hints: Equate line and curve: $x^2 - 4x + 3 = mx - 6 \implies x^2 - (m + 4)x + 9 = 0$.
Set the discriminant $\Delta = (m + 4)^2 - 36 = 0$ to find $m = 2$ and $m = -10$.
Substitute each value of $m$ to determine the corresponding coordinates of contact.
walkthrough:
Equate the tangent line and quadratic curve equations:
$$x^2 - 4x + 3 = mx - 6 \implies x^2 - (m + 4)x + 9 = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = 0$:
$$(m + 4)^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0 \implies (m + 4)^2 = 36$$
$$m + 4 = \pm 6 \implies m = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -10$$

Find the point of contact for $m = 2$:
$$x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0 \implies (x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = 3$$
$$y = 2(3) - 6 = 0 \implies (3, 0)$$

Find the point of contact for $m = -10$:
$$x^2 + 6x + 9 = 0 \implies (x + 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = -3$$
$$y = -10(-3) - 6 = 24 \implies (-3, 24)$$

ai_rubric.Tangents and Normals: Forms $x^2 - (m + 4)x + 9 = 0$ (M1). Sets discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = 0$ (DM1). Obtains $m = 2, -10$ (A1). Substitutes $m$ into quadratic (DM1). Obtains $(3, 0)$ (A1) and $(-3, 24)$ (A1).
